title: SDK parity audit epic: auth, retries/backoff, timeouts, streaming semantics (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Monica Patel

Context / why:
We’re seeing recurring customer friction where behavior differs between SDKs ("works in TS but not in Python"), plus intermittent production failures due to mismatched defaults for timeouts and retry behavior (429/5xx handling, Retry-After support, stream disconnect semantics). This epic tracks the end-to-end parity initiative to align Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK behavior around:
- Auth resolution (explicit param vs env vars) and secret handling/redaction
- Retry policy (retryable errors/codes, backoff+jitter, Retry-After, max attempts)
- Timeout model (connect/read/overall semantics and defaults)
- Streaming behavior (disconnect handling, partial output semantics, retry guidance + idempotency)
- Error taxonomy and typed errors with request_id surfaced consistently
- Shared conformance test suite + fixtures
- Docs, quickstarts, migration notes, and release checklist

Goals (deliverables):
1) Parity audit matrix
- Capture current vs desired behavior across Python/TS/Go for auth precedence, default timeouts, retryable errors, backoff/jitter, max attempts, streaming edge cases, and error typing.
- Include acceptance criteria and open questions.

2) Publish a single standard (approved by SRE + Security + PM)
- Auth resolution order + env var names
- Retry policy + Retry-After handling + max attempts
- Timeout model + defaults
- Streaming semantics + conservative retry guidance
- Typed errors + fields (request_id, status_code, retryable)

3) Implementation across SDKs
- Align behavior and config knobs
- Add consistent logging/telemetry fields (or hooks) where permitted
- Add conformance test suite and require in CI

4) Docs + examples + migration notes
- Consistent naming and recommended defaults across all docs/quickstarts
- Clear migration guidance and deprecation notes

Non-goals / out of scope:
- Major API redesign or new auth mechanisms
- Deep model semantics changes
- Gateway changes beyond consistency signals (e.g., Retry-After/header consistency, stable error code fields)

Acceptance criteria (definition of done for epic):
- All three SDKs implement the standardized auth resolution order and env var names; deprecated names emit warnings (where supported).
- All three SDKs implement retry policy v1:
  - Retryable: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 + network/transient errors
  - Not retryable: 4xx (except 429) by default
  - Respect Retry-After (seconds + HTTP-date)
  - Jittered exponential backoff
  - Configurable max attempts and overall cap
- Timeout model is aligned across SDKs, including streaming vs non-streaming behavior; defaults are documented and consistent.
- Typed error taxonomy implemented across SDKs with request_id available in all errors (including streaming disconnects).
- Streaming: partial output semantics are consistent; disconnect produces a typed error with a clear retryability signal and retry guidance.
- Conformance suite exists and gates CI for each SDK with shared fixtures for 429/Retry-After and simulated network failures.
- Docs/quickstarts/migration notes published and cross-linked; release checklist executed.

Milestones (target ~8 weeks):
Week 1–2: Audit & data gathering
- Publish parity matrix and top support drivers
- Draft standards/RFC text and circulate for review

Week 2–3: Design & approval
- Publish ADRs for retry policy + timeout model
- Security review sign-off for auth resolution + secret handling
- Decide migration strategy (feature flags vs minor version default shifts)

Week 3–6: Implementation
- Python/TS/Go PRs for auth/retry/timeout/streaming and error taxonomy
- Conformance tests + fixtures integrated in each repo CI
- Update docs/examples in parallel

Week 6–8: Rollout & validation
- Beta releases for all SDKs; dogfood internally and with a small set of customers
- Monitor retry rate/timeout rate/stream disconnect reasons; confirm no retry storms
- Publish GA releases, migration notes, support playbook; run retro

Current status (as of 2026-02-27):
- Standards/ADRs: Drafted and in final review with SRE + Security; last open item is final default timeout values for streaming vs non-streaming and how we message the change in migration notes.
- Platform dependency (ENG-5130): Gateway work in progress to ensure Retry-After on 429 is consistent and request_id/error fields are always present (streaming + non-streaming).
- SDK implementation: In active PR phase across all three language repos; conformance harness integration underway.
- Docs: In progress; waiting for final option names/fields from ENG-5126 to avoid churn.

Risks + mitigations:
- Retry storms / thundering herd under elevated 429s:
  - Mitigation: capped attempts, respect Retry-After, jitter, and staged rollout with monitoring + rollback triggers.
- Breaking behavior changes for existing customers (timeouts/retries):
  - Mitigation: deprecations, migration guide, and where needed opt-in flags before default flips.
- Streaming retries causing duplicate side effects:
  - Mitigation: conservative guidance; do not auto-retry mid-stream by default; emphasize idempotency keys and request_id logging.
- Secret exposure in logs:
  - Mitigation: redaction requirements, safe error messages, security review gate before GA.

Rollout checklist (high-level):
- [ ] Conformance tests passing for Python/TS/Go on main
- [ ] Gateway emits Retry-After on 429 and stable error fields required by SDK taxonomy
- [ ] Beta releases cut (all 3 SDKs within 48 hours)
- [ ] Dashboards live: retry_rate, timeout_rate, stream_disconnect_reason, request_id coverage
- [ ] Support playbook + macros updated
- [ ] Migration notes published + linked from docs site
- [ ] GA releases + announcement + changelogs
- [ ] Retro completed; file follow-ups for any remaining parity gaps

Notes for oncall/support:
When customers report intermittent failures, request:
- SDK name + version
- request_id from error output (should be present in new typed errors)
- Whether request was streaming
- Config: max_attempts, timeout model (overall vs connect/read), and any proxy/VPN details

Owner reminders:
- SDK owners: please keep option names aligned (snake_case vs camelCase is ok, but semantics and defaults must match). Do not introduce language-specific default behaviors without explicit sign-off in ENG-5126 comment thread.
- Please link PRs directly in the relevant sub-issues and update this epic only at milestone boundaries (to keep noise down).
